title: Observation
description: Something learned about how a GraphCompose line actually behaves, discovered while building a template and confirmed by a probe. An observation is NOT a skill: it is evidence, held apart from the versioned skill packs until a probe re-confirms it and it is deliberately promoted. Written to stop the next run rediscovering what this one paid for.

id.description: Stable kebab-case id, also the filename. Reused across revisions and runs so the same behaviour is not recorded twice under two names.

graphComposeVersion.description: The exact build this was observed against. A behaviour is only claimed for the version that produced it.

api.description: The API surface the behaviour concerns, e.g. ShapeContainerBuilder.margin. Used to find the observation from the call being written.

observedBehaviour.description: What actually happens, stated as fact and in the terms someone hitting it would search for. Not what should happen.

probe.description: The probe under tools/diagnostics that settles this, e.g. shape-paint. An observation with no probe cannot be re-confirmed and must not be promoted.

arrangement.description: The smallest arrangement that shows it, in one sentence.

probeResult.description: The numbers the probe reported when this was recorded. `observations verify` re-runs the probe and compares against these, which is how a library fix retires an observation rather than leaving it to mislead.

workaround.description: What to do instead, derived from the measurement rather than tuned by eye. Empty when the behaviour is simply a fact to know.

confidence.description: suspected: seen once, no probe agreement yet. confirmed: a probe reproduces it on demand. retired: the library changed and the probe no longer reproduces it — kept so the next reader knows it was checked, not forgotten.

sourceRun.description: Where it was first paid for. Not provenance for its own sake: a behaviour found once in one document is weaker evidence than one found in three.

promotedTo.description: The skill-pack file this was folded into, once a probe confirmed it and someone decided it belongs in the pack. Null means it is still only evidence. Promotion is deliberate — an observation added to a skill automatically would be an unverified claim presented as the API contract.

engineDefect.description: Set when the behaviour is a defect in GraphCompose rather than a design limit. The distinction decides what happens to the workaround: a limit is permanent guidance, a defect is scaffolding that must be removed when the engine is fixed. An observation carrying this must never be promoted into a pack for a later line without re-running its probe against that line.

affectedVersions.description: The versions known to carry it, e.g. "2.2.0" or "2.0.0-2.2.0".

reportedTo.description: Issue or discussion where it was raised upstream, or null if not yet raised.

fixedIn.description: The GraphCompose version that fixes it, once known. While null, the workaround stands; once set, this observation should be retired for that line and the workaround removed rather than carried forward.

retiredNote.description: Why this stopped holding, and what was measured instead. `confidence: retired` records that an observation is no longer true and, on its own, records nothing about why — which is the drift this whole system exists to prevent. Name the version that changed it and quote the probe values that moved, so a reader on the older line can still tell whether the workaround applies to them.

version.description: The exact GraphCompose build the probe ran against, including any -SNAPSHOT suffix. A snapshot is not its release and must be recorded as itself.

on.description: ISO date the probe was re-run.

verdict.description: held: the probe reproduced what this record claims. changed: it did not, which is what retiring an observation should rest on.

note.description: What moved, when the verdict is `changed`.

verifiedAgainst.description: Every build this record has actually been measured against, newest last. `graphComposeVersion` says where it was FIRST seen and `sourceRun` says who paid for it; neither answers "is it true on the build in front of me", which is the only question a reader has. A record retired against 2.2.1 was believed by a project pinned to 2.2.1-SNAPSHOT — the line before 2.2.1 ships — and the restriction it described was still live. Listing the builds explicitly makes an unmeasured version visibly unmeasured instead of silently covered.

allOf.description: A retired observation has to say what retired it.
